Job Requirements

The AI Supercomputing team at Siemens Healthineers is looking for a Senior HPC Systems Administrator to support the day-to-day operation of Sherlock, our enterprise AI supercomputing platform.
 

Sherlock powers AI research and development across medical imaging, diagnostics, and foundation model initiatives. The environment includes NVIDIA GPU clusters, high-speed InfiniBand networking, petabyte-scale storage, and Slurm workload management.
 

This is a hands-on operations role focused on maintaining system reliability, resolving production issues, and ensuring a high-quality user experience. You will work closely with the engineering team responsible for infrastructure architecture and future platform enhancements.
 

Key Responsibilities


HPC Operations
•    Administer and maintain a large-scale Linux-based HPC environment.
•    Monitor system health, troubleshoot issues, and ensure high availability.
•    Perform OS maintenance, patching, upgrades, and configuration management.
•    Conduct capacity planning, preventive maintenance, and system health checks.
•    Maintain operational documentation and configuration records.
 

Slurm & GPU Administration
•    Manage Slurm scheduling, resource allocation, and job accounting.
•    Troubleshoot job failures, performance issues, and scheduling problems.
•    Monitor and support NVIDIA GPU infrastructure, including hardware, drivers, and CUDA-related services.
•    Support researchers and engineers with workload execution issues.
 

Storage & Network Support
•    Monitor and troubleshoot storage, networking, and connectivity issues.
•    Coordinate incident resolution with internal teams and external vendors.
•    Support parallel file systems, backup, recovery, and data integrity processes.
•    Help investigate network performance and infrastructure bottlenecks.
 

Monitoring & Automation
•    Improve monitoring, alerting, and operational health checks.
•    Automate routine administration tasks using Bash, Python, Ansible, or similar tools.
•    Perform root-cause analysis and implement long-term fixes for recurring issues.
•    Maintain incident response and service recovery procedures.
•    Produce operational and reliability reports.
 

Incident Management & User Support
•    Respond to and resolve production incidents across Linux, HPC, storage, and network systems.
•    Communicate system status and incident impacts to stakeholders.
•    Support users with cluster access, development environments, and software environments.
•    Escalate complex infrastructure issues when needed.
 

Collaboration
•    Partner with the AI Supercomputing Engineering team to ensure reliable platform operations.
•    Support the transition of new infrastructure into production.
•    Provide operational feedback on reliability, supportability, and maintainability.
•    Assist with testing and implementation activities while maintaining focus on production operations.
 



Work Experience

•    Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, IT, or equivalent experience.
•    5+ years of Linux system administration experience, ideally in HPC, research computing, or large-scale compute environments.
•    Strong Linux troubleshooting skills, including networking, storage, system services, and kernel diagnostics.
•    Experience with Slurm or a similar workload manager.
•    Experience managing Linux server clusters.
•    Familiarity with NVIDIA GPU hardware, drivers, and monitoring.
•    Knowledge of distributed storage systems and high-performance networking (TCP/IP, InfiniBand, RDMA).
•    Scripting and automation experience (Bash, Python, or similar).
•    Proven ability to resolve complex production issues, perform root-cause analysis, and maintain reliable operations.
•    Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and own production system stability.

 

Preferred Qualifications
•    Experience with HPC management platforms such as NVIDIA Base Command Manager, Bright Cluster Manager, or Open OnDemand.
•    Experience with distributed file systems (e.g., Ceph, Lustre, BeeGFS, VAST Data, IBM Spectrum Scale).
•    Experience with NVIDIA DGX/HGX and multi-GPU environments.
•    Knowledge of InfiniBand administration and troubleshooting.
•    Familiarity with Slurm resource scheduling, accounting, and performance analysis.
•    Experience with monitoring tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, NVIDIA DCGM.
•    Knowledge of Linux access management, SSH, and enterprise authentication.
•    Experience supporting containers (Apptainer/Singularity) and Python/Conda environments.
•    Familiarity with remote development tools and operational processes such as incident management and change control.
